context.body: Distinction, divine identity, creation, incarnation, grace, and revelation are held in compressed poetic claims.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: The prologue distinguishes the Word as with God, calls the Word God, attributes creation and life to him, and says the Word became flesh and made the unseen God known.
observations.label: The Word is with God and is God: action

observations.body: Witnesses receive or reject the light; believers become God’s children.
observations.label: The Word is with God and is God: response

observations.body: in the beginning · with God · was God · became flesh · made him known

payload.posture: Read John 1:1–18 as jesus names the father evidence before carrying it into another source.
payload.tension: The Greek wording distinguishes “the Word” and “God” while making a direct predication that resists either simple identity or separation.
payload.title: The Word is with God and is God
